in_text_mentions: We aimed to reduce the intermetatarsal angle to 7°. One mm of rotation equals 1° of correction which could be measured by the amount of overhanging bone of the superior fragment once the metatarsal head was rotated. The bone fragments were held with a scarf clamp and fixed with two 2.0 cortical screws using AO technique (Figures 6 and 7). The overhanging edges of bone were then removed from the medial side of the metatarsal shaft. An Akin closing wedge osteotomy of the proximal phalanx was performed on all cases. The Akin osteotomy was fixated using a single 1.2 mm threaded k-wire (Figure 7).
